title: Trust in AI among Middle Eastern CS Students: Investigating Students’ Trust and Usage Patterns Across Saudi Arabia, Kuwait and Jordan

bias_targets.methodology: Comparing survey responses on AI trust, usage, and adoption patterns across three Middle Eastern countries (Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Jordan) to evaluate how regional cultural environments and educational systems affect AI interaction compared to WEIRD (Western, Educated, Industrialized, Rich, and Democratic) populations.
Measuring disparities in AI trust, confidence, and perceived learning outcomes between male and female computer science students using Likert-scale surveys and Wilcoxon rank-sum tests.
Evaluating the impact of English language barriers on students' confidence and trust in AI tools using self-reported survey responses and Pearson correlation analysis.
Assessing differences in self-reliance, AI trust levels, and usage behaviors between first-generation and continuing-generation university students through comparative survey analysis.
